item.title: The Alarm Worked
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: The company removed the only canary that actually signaled danger. Now they leave the empty cage on the wall to prove they are still watching.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"The Alarm Worked"
❓ They killed the alarm because it was too loud. That gives them plausible deniability: the oversight gear is still on the wall.
AND: The canary kept dying every time the air got bad. Instead of fixing the air, the bosses took the bird out and called it a process fix to stop the noise. The cage is empty now. They left the labels on the wall so they can tell the board the mine is still being monitored. The alarm worked. That was the problem.

item.title: The Invisible Prototype
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Why a 1920s discovery was buried for decades. The specific social camouflage that hides autism in plain sight. How standard diagnostic tests ignore female-typical interests. The hidden cost of being mislabeled for a lifetime.
item.sync:pageSocial:
The Invisible Prototype
When diagnostic tools only catch loud disruption, quiet compensation looks like the absence of autism.
✜ Boys became the blueprint Autism research rests on a narrow history marked by gender bias. In the 1920s, Grunya Sukhareva detailed how autism presented in both boys and girls. That evidence vanished as later researchers built a male-dominated canon. Asperger's influential work relied on a tiny sample of only four boys. Autism hardened into a boy's experience, and female presentations fell out of view.
✜ Jack gets flagged; Chloe gets "quirks" A teacher sees Jack disrupt the classroom and flags him for assessment. In the next seat, Chloe sits quietly, follows every social cue, and stays in her books. Tools hunt disruptive patterns or intense, isolated interests like trains or mechanical parts. A deep focus on animals or specific authors often fails to count. Criteria catch "acting out" and miss quiet intensity. Anyone who keeps social order stays invisible to the diagnostic machine.
✜ Camouflage buys belonging and spends the self Pressure to belong pushes many autistic women into constant camouflage. A girl may buy the "wrong" My Little Pony just to stay in the group; a small survival move that scales into lifelong masking. Masking hides autism from doctors and bills her for years. Without the right label, many face inappropriate treatments for anxiety or eating disorders, trading mental health for a seat at a table where they are never truly understood.
Loud signals are not the whole spectrum. Ask of any checklist: does it measure the condition, or how loudly the condition shows?

item.title: 🧠 Why does a healthy brain forget your keys?
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Lost keys and blank names usually mean you never paid enough attention for the brain to encode the moment into a stored memory. Most everyday lapses are distraction at that moment. You cannot retrieve a parking spot you never looked at. Alzheimer’s can run silently for years in the hippocampus, the region that binds sensory pieces into new memories. Early signs are failing to form new memories and not knowing how you …
item.sync:pageSocial:
🧠 Why does a healthy brain forget your keys?
Lost keys and a blank name after 40 feel like early Alzheimer's. Lisa Genova says a healthy brain was never built to catalog every name or parking spot. A memory champion who memorized 111,000 digits of pi still forgot a birthday.
✜ Distraction, not a broken store You cannot retrieve what you never looked at. Encoding is the moment attention becomes a memory. Phones and feeds steal that second before the circuit starts. Googling a missing word leaves the store intact. Search is an open-book test, not digital amnesia.
✜ Names live in a cul-de-sac Proper nouns have few routes in. A baker's job (apron, oven, smell) has thousands. The occupation sticks; the surname does not. Remembering to do something later fails by design. Pilots lower the wheels with a checklist.
✜ Lost keys vs lost arrival Alzheimer's starts in the hippocampus and can run silently for 15 to 20 years. Normal forgetting is misplacing keys. The disease is failing to recognize your car, or not knowing how you arrived. For about 98% of people, sleep, walking, diet, new learning, and unmanaged chronic stress change whether sticky protein plaques hit a tipping point. Extra neural routes still work when one path is blocked.
Everyday forgetting tracks attention. Alzheimer's tracks a slow plaque clock.

item.dc:creator: xynova

item.sync:pageSocial:
"Tiene cara de yo no fui."
❓ You see feigned innocence against undeniable evidence, a "Who, me?" face when the mess is obvious. You use it when a kid stands by a broken lamp looking angelic, or when a friend denies eating the last slice of pizza with crumbs on their chin.
AND: The guiltier the party, the wider the eyes. You hear this when a roommate leaves an empty milk carton in the fridge and acts completely bewildered when you point it out. It also comes up when a colleague accidentally CCs a client on an internal rant and suddenly acts like they do not know how email threads work.

item.title: 🧠 Why can the same ADD medicine ruin one brain and save another?
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Many clinics diagnose ADD from symptom checklists without looking at the brain at all. The same stimulant that helps Classic ADD (underactive frontal lobes) can worsen Ring of Fire ADD (an overactive pattern). A “depression” pill for Inattentive ADD can push frontal function lower and tip into dangerous disinhibition.
item.sync:pageSocial:
🧠 Why can the same ADD medicine ruin one brain and save another?
Diagnosing ADD from symptom checklists alone is like asking a mechanic to fix an engine by listening to the sounds and never opening the hood. Psychiatrists who never look at the brain work the same way. Different activity patterns can look like the same disorder, and a one-size pill leaves many without the attention they require.
✜ Same label, opposite brains Classic ADD and many inattentive cases show low frontal activity. Stimulants can help that underactive pattern. Overfocused and Ring of Fire patterns sit on the other side: stuck, overactive circuitry. Stimulants can pour fuel on that fire.
✜ Wrong chemistry can look like help A pastor's wife with inattentive ADD was treated as depression and given Prozac. For her underactive frontal pattern, the drug pushed function lower and tipped into public disinhibition at a stoplight. Imaging, stopping the Prozac, and a targeted stimulant ended the crisis.
What matters is what is happening inside your head, and how you bring that pattern under control: match the plan to the brain you have, not a one-size ADD pill. When meds keep failing, ask for practitioners who use objective brain imaging and build from the scan, not the checklist alone.

item.title: 🤝 Why does conquest start with a partnership?
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Rome, in Johnathan Bi’s reading of Machiavelli, conquered by inviting neighbors as junior partners: they kept their laws and rulers, and they fought the next wars as proxies. Fraud did the scaling: Rome used those partners to take the next cities, then turned the partners into subjects once the work was done. A pyramid sales scheme runs the same invite at human scale: you keep your name and pitch, recruit the next …
item.sync:pageSocial:
🤝 Why does conquest start with a partnership?
Johnathan Bi on Machiavelli: Rome opened with an invite.
✜ Junior partner, not equal Nearby cities kept their laws and rulers, joined as junior partners, and fought Rome's next war as proxies. The public story was alliance; the military fact was proxy war.
✜ Force costs too much A league of equals stalls in committee; the UN still ends headlines with "restraint." Direct occupation burns treasure and breeds rebellion. Fraud scales: keep the costume of alliance while proxies take the hits.
✜ Then the partner becomes the subject Rome used those partners to take the next cities, then turned the partners into subjects while still looking like a friend. After Sparta won, it collapsed under an empire its closed design could not run.
A pyramid sales scheme still runs the same invite: you keep your name and pitch, then recruit the next ring, and the people above you live off that expansion while your recruits become the next proxies.
Nukes make classic land-grabs suicidal, so expansion shifts to buyouts and tech. In Bi's joke version of the old fraud, you cheat investors instead of junior partners.
If you keep your laws, logo, or title while someone else sets the next campaign and your people carry the cost, you are the junior partner in someone else's conquest: a proxy with a friendly contract.

item.title: El que se va sin que lo boten, regresa sin que lo llamen.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A figure with a suitcase walks away, then hesitantly peeks back through the door. People who leave on their own often return without an invite.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"El que se va sin que lo boten, regresa sin que lo llamen."
❓ You give up your standing when you walk out by choice. Then you lose your leverage if you try to return uninvited. A voluntary exit costs you power if you ever try to return. Imagine an employee who resigns, then seeks re-employment. Or a partner who leaves a relationship, then tries to reconcile uninvited. They come back now on their terms, not yours.
AND: You recognize it as the quiet DM months later, or the classic warning whispered by family. A former colleague who quit in a huff quietly slides into your DMs, asking if the old role is still open. Family members also whisper a warning after a relative cuts ties over a minor dispute, only to show up at Thanksgiving dinner as if nothing happened.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • You will come crawling back. • They always come back. • The grass is not always greener.

item.title: Stability Is a Setting
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Red Impulsiveness and Reality Detachment get handled as a messaging problem first. The public readout is updated so the board deck can still show Leadership Confidence: Stable.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Stability Is a Setting"
❓ Red warning gauges get treated as a comms problem so early structural change can wait. Continuity is cheaper than correction, so by the time a real fix arrives, the gap between the public story and day-to-day reality is already wide.
AND: When the Grandiosity Gauges show high impulsiveness, the first move is usually to update the public readout. Grandiose thinking gets reframed as strategic intent so the board deck can match last quarter. Keeping the current leadership costs less, short term, than opening a search. The board can file the red needles under communication risk rather than leadership failure, which delays the audit. When correction finally arrives, it is often a late restructure after Leadership Confidence: Stable has already bought time.
